message.content:
Below is a quick‑look list of the **federal statutory holidays that create a long weekend in Canada in 2023**.  
(If you’re planning trips for a specific province or territory, keep in mind that each jurisdiction has its own set of holidays that may add or shift long weekends.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend Span (including the holiday) |
|---------|-------------|-------------|-------------------------------------------|
| **Family Day** (Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Ontario, New Brunswick, Manitoba, Prince Edward Island) | Feb 20 | Monday | Feb 18–20 |
| **Good Friday** | Apr 7 | Friday | Apr 7–9 |
| **Victoria Day** | May 22 | Monday | May 20–22 |
| **Labour Day** | Sep 4 | Monday | Sep 2–4 |
| **Thanksgiving** | Oct 9 | Monday | Oct 7–9 |
| **Remembrance Day** (observed in some provinces) | Nov 11 | Monday | Nov 9–11 |
| **Christmas Day** | Dec 25 | Monday | Dec 23–25 |

### Quick notes

* **New Year’s Day** (Jan 1, Sunday) and **Canada Day** (Jul 1, Saturday) fall on weekends, so they don’t create an extra day off unless you take a day off in between.
* **Boxing Day** (Dec 26, Tuesday) is a federal holiday but does not create a long weekend on its own.
* Some provinces observe **Family Day** on a different date or have additional holidays (e.g., **St. Patrick’s Day** in Newfoundland & Labrador, **St. George’s Day** in Prince Edward Island, **St. John’s Day** in Newfoundland & Labrador, etc.).  
  If you need the full provincial list, let me know which province(s) you’re interested in.

Feel free to copy this table into your holiday‑planning app, or let me know if you’d like a more detailed breakdown for a particular province!
